prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1072; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Received first notice of loss from insured by phone. Low-speed head-on collision at an intersection, both vehicles driven at low speed. Insured reports neck pain and stiffness, no airbag deployment. Police report requested. Photos of both vehicles requested from insured.

Entry 2: Claimant's attorney's office contacted by letter confirming representation. All further communication to go through counsel. Claimant is not to be contacted directly. Preliminary liability appears disputed; other driver's carrier notified and acknowledgment pending.

Entry 3: Reviewed photos and repair estimate for claimant vehicle. Front bumper, hood, and radiator support damage consistent with reported impact. Independent appraisal scheduled. Medical authorization forms sent to attorney's office for records request.

Entry 4: Claimant's attorney submitted initial treatment summary. Diagnosis listed as cervical and lumbar strain. Chiropractic and physical therapy noted. Treatment ongoing. Requested complete records and billing itemization before evaluating bodily injury component.

Entry 5: Liability position under review with supervisor. Recorded statement from insured obtained and filed. Awaiting other carrier's response and complete medical records before setting reserves. Diary set for follow-up with counsel.
